title: Will My Cat Eat My Eyeballs? And Other Questions About Dead Bodies
author: Caitlin Doughty
target_audience: Adults and older teens curious about death and mortuary practices
Readers interested in science, biology, and human anatomy
People with questions about what really happens to bodies after death
Followers of Caitlin Doughty and death-positive movement
core_themes: Cultural and historical perspectives on death and funerals
Debunking myths and taboos about corpses
Honest conversations about mortality for all ages
primary_purpose: To provide accessible, often humorous, scientifically accurate answers to unusual and frequently macabre questions about death and dead bodies, demystifying mortality and encouraging curiosity and openness about a traditionally taboo topic.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, witty, and direct; uses a Q&A format based on real reader questions—often from children.
structure_format.organization: Arranged as a series of short chapters, each responding to a specific question about death or dead bodies.
features: Inclusion of scientific facts, historical anecdotes, and cultural practices
Often uses humor or surprising analogies to explain concepts

key_concepts_lessons: Death is both a biological event and a cultural phenomenon, surrounded by myth and misinformation.
Many common fears and morbid questions about corpses have surprisingly straightforward, sometimes mundane, answers.
The decomposition process is fascinating, complex, and natural.
Funeral practices vary widely across cultures and history.
It's healthy and important to ask questions about death, especially for children.
Demystifying death can reduce fear and stigma.
notable_features: Draws on the author's experience as a mortician and funeral director
Based on real questions, many from children
Combines scientific facts with humor and storytelling
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2019 amidst a growing 'death positive' movement encouraging more open discussion about mortality, funerals, and body disposition. The book responds to a societal shift toward curiosity and transparency about end-of-life issues, especially among younger generations.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller, praised for making difficult topics accessible and engaging
Popular among fans of Mary Roach and similar science communicators
Critically acclaimed for its blend of humor, empathy, and fact-based answers
Helped normalize open conversations about death, especially with young people
Some found the subject matter unsettling, but many appreciated its candor
comparable_titles: Smoke Gets in Your Eyes: And Other Lessons from the Crematory by Caitlin Doughty
Stiff: The Curious Lives of Human Cadavers by Mary Roach
From Here to Eternity: Traveling the World to Find the Good Death by Caitlin Doughty
The Ultimate Book of Funeral Etiquette by Jeanne Hamilton
